plans.note: Section 21 is the operative cap; check mutuality, cap multiple/measure (Fees paid vs payable), exclusion of indirect damages and the 'Excluded Claims' carve-out set defined in Section 1 and cross-referenced from the indemnity in Section 20.

Section 20 should carry Vendor IP-infringement and misconduct indemnities plus procedure/control; confirm any Customer-side indemnity is narrow and that Section 21 does not cap the Vendor indemnity below the Excluded Claims treatment.

No non-compete heading; scan Customer Responsibilities, Compliance and General for any restraint on the businesses we run or competing products we may buy or build before concluding absent (absence is favourable — no redline).
Check Agreement Structure/Scope and Order Forms for sole-source or 'all requirements' language; likely absent, and absence favours us.
Direction rule: only flag if Fees/Order Form terms oblige us to give Vendor our best terms or most-favoured pricing; an MFN running in our favour is welcome and not redlined.
Non-solicits often sit in General or alongside confidentiality; if present, test duration (≤12 months), scope (personnel actually engaged) and a general-advertising/unsolicited-response carve-out.

Section 9 governs termination rights; confirm Customer may terminate for convenience on reasonable notice without penalty/early-termination fee, and that Vendor has no symmetrical mid-term convenience exit.
Section 8 covers term and auto-renewal; check the non-renewal notice window length and any renewal uplift, with Section 7 for the pricing/escalator mechanics.
Section 28 sets law, venue and any arbitration; verify law is NY/DE/CA/England & Wales and that disputes go to courts rather than foreign-seated arbitration.
Section 24 addresses assignment and change of control; confirm we may assign to Affiliates and to a successor without consent, and that Vendor cannot terminate on our change of control.

Section 14 allocates Deliverable ownership and Section 15 Customer Data; ensure no assignment or broad licence of our IP/data to Vendor beyond what is needed to deliver the Services, and check any feedback/aggregated-data grant.
Section 13 is the access/licence grant; test that it extends to Affiliates and contractors, is not revocable at will, and is coextensive with the Order Form scope.

Section 22 is the Vendor's audit of our usage; check frequency, prior written notice, business-hours/off-site conduct, and that Vendor bears cost absent a material underpayment. Section 23 may hold our reciprocal assurance rights (do not flag those).
Direction rule: service credits payable to us in the SLA (Section 3) are welcome; look in Fees (Section 7) for late-payment penalties or liquidated damages running against us and only flag those.
Section 19 holds the performance warranty; check duration, the re-perform/refund remedy, and whether any disclaimer guts it. Section 6 acceptance and Section 3 service levels are related remedies.
Section 18 exists; verify lines and limits (commercial general, professional/E&O, cyber) and evidence-of-coverage obligations given Vendor hosts Customer Data.

Order Forms (Section 4) and Fees (Section 7) are where any minimum volume or take-or-pay commitment would sit; if present, confirm there is an exit or reduction right rather than an unconditional commitment.
Section 11 covers transition assistance and data return; check the assistance period, rates, export format and deletion timing, read with the effect-of-termination provisions in Section 10.
